Book.title: Book
Book.description: Represents a single book in the library catalog.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Book entity.

author.description: The author or authors of the book.

isbn.description: The International Standard Book Number (ISBN) for the book.

category.description: The genre or category of the book (e.g., Fiction, Science, History).

totalCopies.description: The total number of physical copies of this book owned by the library.

availableCopies.description: The number of copies of this book currently available for borrowing.

location.description: The physical location or shelf number of the book within the library.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the book record was initially created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the book record was last updated.

Member.title: Member
Member.description: Represents a library member, including both students and librarians (admins).

id.description: Unique identifier for the Member entity.

name.description: The full name of the library member.

email.description: The email address of the library member, used for login and notifications.

memberId.description: A unique identifier assigned to the member, potentially for external systems or physical library cards.

phone.description: The phone number of the library member.

role.description: The role of the member within the application (e.g., 'admin' for librarians, 'user' for students).

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the member record was initially created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the member record was last updated.

Transaction.title: Transaction
Transaction.description: Records details of a book being issued to or returned by a member.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Transaction entity.

bookId.description: Reference to the Book involved in this transaction. (Relationship: Book 1:N Transaction)

memberId.description: Reference to the Member who initiated this transaction. (Relationship: Member 1:N Transaction)

issueDate.description: Date and time when the book was issued.

dueDate.description: Date and time when the book is due for return.

returnDate.description: Date and time when the book was actually returned. Null if not yet returned.

status.description: The current status of the transaction (e.g., 'issued', 'returned').

fineAmount.description: The calculated fine amount for late returns, if any.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the transaction record was initially created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the transaction record was last updated.

definition.description: Collection for all books in the library catalog. This collection has a public read security posture, allowing all users (authenticated or unauthenticated) to search and view book details. Write operations (create, update, delete) are restricted to administrators. No authorization dependencies on other documents.

params.name: bookId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific book.

definition.description: Collection for all library members (students and librarians). Each document's ID is the Firebase Authentication UID of the member. Users can read and update their own document, while administrators have full read/write access to all member documents. This path supports Authorization Independence by matching `request.auth.uid` to `userId` in the path.

params.name: userId
params.description: The Firebase Authentication UID of the library member.

definition.description: Collection storing records of book lending and returns. Each document includes denormalized `memberId` and `bookId` fields to ensure Authorization Independence. Members can read only their own transactions (where `resource.data.memberId` matches `request.auth.uid`), supporting QAPs. Administrators have full read/write access to all transactions.

params.name: transactionId
params.description: The unique identifier for a specific book transaction.

definition.description: A dedicated collection for Database-Backed Access Control (DBAC). The document ID (`adminId`) corresponds to a Firebase Authentication UID, indicating that the associated member has administrative privileges. This collection enables fast, secure rule-based authorization checks using `exists()`, ensuring Authorization Independence for global roles. Documents in this collection typically serve as marker flags and may contain minimal data, linking implicitly to a Member with an 'admin' role.

params.name: adminId
params.description: The Firebase Authentication UID of an administrator.

firestore.reasoning: The Firestore data structure for Catalogify is designed with a strong emphasis on Authorization Independence, Structural Segregation, and Query as Permissions (QAPs) to ensure a secure, scalable, and debuggable backend. Authorization Independence (CRITICAL): 1. Books (`/books/{bookId}`): Access to books does not depend on any parent or related document's data. Public read access for the catalog is allowed for all, and write access is strictly limited to authenticated administrators. This removes any need for `get()` calls within security rules for this collection. 2. Members (`/members/{userId}`): A user's profile document is stored directly at `/members/{request.auth.uid}`, making ownership explicit and atomic. User-specific read/write permissions are granted by comparing `request.auth.uid` with the document ID (`userId`). Administrator access is determined by checking for existence in the dedicated `/roles_admin` collection, avoiding cross-document reads (`get()`) on the Member's own 'role' field for primary authorization. This ensures that a Member document can be created/updated atomically without needing to first read a parent or role document. 3. Transactions (`/transactions/{transactionId}`): Each transaction document directly includes `memberId` and `bookId` fields. This denormalization is crucial for authorization independence. A user's ability to read their transactions is determined by comparing `request.auth.uid` directly with `resource.data.memberId`. Similarly, administrator access is validated through the `/roles_admin` collection. This design eliminates any `get()` calls to `/members` or `/books` from `transactions` security rules, supporting atomic operations and simpler rule logic. 4. Global Roles (`/roles_admin/{adminId}`): This collection is used purely for DBAC (Database-Backed Access Control) via existence checks (`exists(/databases/$(database)/documents/roles_admin/$(request.auth.uid))`). It inherently provides authorization independence as it's a direct, atomic check without relying on data within the `adminId` document itself, or any other document's fields. Query as Permissions (QAPs): 1. Books (`/books/{bookId}`): The entire collection is publicly readable, enabling the 'Searchable Public Catalog (OPAC)' feature for all users, including unauthenticated ones. This allows secure `list` queries (e.g., `collection('books').where('title', '==', '...')`) by anyone, as the security rule `allow read: true;` (or similar) permits it for all documents, eliminating the need for client-side filtering and making the rule a true permission. 2. Members (`/members/{userId}`): While individual users can `get` their own profile, `list` queries on the `/members` collection are restricted to administrators. This is a secure QAP as administrators can `list` all members because their role grants them full access, and regular users cannot list other members. 3. Transactions (`/transactions/{transactionId}`): This collection fully supports QAPs for members. A member can securely query for their borrowed books using `db.collection('transactions').where('memberId', '==', request.auth.uid)`. The security rule `allow read: if resource.data.memberId == request.auth.uid;` will perfectly match this query, ensuring only the authenticated user's transactions are returned, without exposing others. Administrators, by virtue of their role, can securely `list` all transactions. Structural Segregation: Each collection (`/books`, `/members`, `/transactions`, `/roles_admin`) maintains a homogeneous security posture. For example, all documents in `/books` are publicly readable, while all documents in `/transactions` are either readable by the owning member or any admin. There is no mixing of public/private or user/admin-specific data within the same collection, simplifying security rules significantly and enhancing clarity of intent.
